Dear me in June, I am writing this on the second of September.

Then I took a pen and wrote an answer.
"Dear me in September, You were wrong, and I am glad.
This year I have read my first book in English.
It was thin, and it had pictures, but I read it to the end.
I have written to a girl in Canada, who has become my friend.
I have watched a film without subtitles and understood more than half.
I have learned that English is spoken on every continent.
It is the language of the Maori haka and Aboriginal stories, of Scottish mountains and American deserts.
It is used by pilots, scientists and programmers.
If you know it, you can ask the world a question and understand the answer.
Thanks to English, I can tell the world about my country.
When my friend from Canada asked me about Ukraine, I found the words.
